title: Workshop bay with open‑wheeled vehicle chassis and tools
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.
One partially assembled open‑wheeled vehicle (race car chassis/body) occupies the right and central foreground; the bodywork has a pointed nose and a raised roll hoop at the rear of the cockpit area.
One exposed wheel mounted on the vehicle visible at the left side of the chassis (left front/center area of image).
One spare wheel and tire wrapped in plastic on the floor in front of the vehicle (foreground, slightly right of centre).
Two red jack stands visible underneath the vehicle (one near the rear area visible on the right side, one forward near center under chassis).

Three tall stools visible: one with a purple seat near centre-left beside the chassis, one brown stool to the right of the vehicle nose, and one partially visible stool at the extreme left edge of the image.
One metal shelving unit with multiple shelves and storage boxes on the left background.
One vertical teardrop banner/flag on a stand at left foreground.
One red multi-drawer tool chest/cabinet against the left wall (behind the shelving unit).
One large cardboard box on the floor in the foreground left of centre.
A stack of product/retail boxes on a small wheeled cart at far left (multiple boxes stacked; at least three distinct box faces are visible).
One clear or translucent plastic wheeled container/drawer unit on the lower shelf of the shelving unit (left background).
One long white cylindrical tube or roll (white tube) lying on the middle shelf of the shelving unit, protruding to the right.
Overhead suspended cable or cord visible running from the ceiling toward the centre top of the image.
spatial_relations: The open‑wheeled vehicle is positioned across the right and central foreground, facing to the right with its pointed nose near the right edge of the image and the cockpit/roll hoop nearer the centre.

The wrapped spare wheel sits on the floor directly in front of the vehicle nose and slightly right of centre, with a brown stool to its immediate right and the purple stool slightly behind and to the left of the wrapped wheel.
Two red jack stands are located under the vehicle: one visible toward the right/rear under the body and one nearer the centre/front under the chassis.
A shelving unit is located behind the left side of the vehicle (left background), with a red multi-drawer tool chest immediately to the right of that shelving unit against the left wall.
A vertical green teardrop banner stands in front of the shelving unit toward the left foreground, partially obscuring the lower shelves and stacked boxes behind it.
A large cardboard box is on the floor in the foreground left of centre, in front of the stacked boxes and wheeled cart at the far left.
colours_and_materials: The vehicle body appears to be a dark grey/black composite or painted surface with a green stripe or green painted panel on the top midsection and a white section behind the roll hoop.
The teardrop banner is green with white lettering or graphics (text not fully legible).
The jack stands are red; the multi-drawer tool chest is red.
The spare wheel is black with visible yellow/white lettering on the tire tread ('HOOSIER').
Shelving unit appears to be metallic (grey frame) with plastic storage boxes (clear/translucent) on lower shelves.
The floor has two visually distinct surfaces: a grey smooth floor (left foreground) and a tan/brown carpeted rug directly under and around the vehicle area.
uncertainties: Exact room name or number is not visible; therefore location is unknown from image.
Text on the green teardrop banner is partially legible but not certain; only the banner colour is reliably observed. The full banner wording is unreadable from this view.
Many smaller labels, box brand names and printed text on shelving contents and stacked boxes are not legible at this image resolution and have not been transcribed.
Count of stacked boxes on the left wheeled cart is given as at least three visible faces; occlusion prevents a definitive total count of boxes in that stack.
Some stool legs and one stool at the extreme left edge are partially cropped, so the count of three tall stools is the visible count; further stools may be outside the frame.
Material identifications (for example, composite bodywork vs painted metal) are descriptive impressions based on appearance and may be uncertain.
